newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds unchanged in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds unchanged in moderate trade.

text.p: Irish bonds were broadly unchanged in moderate trade on Wednesday as the market continued to lack inspiring data, dealers said.
"Volume has been reasonable today but nothing spectacular," a dealer said. "The market's not going anywhere on the kind of data that's around this week."

Today's market focus was on the UK - retail sales data, minutes of March's monetary meeting and a gilt auction - came out in line with expectations or better than market forecasts, helping sentiment, but having little if any impact on the Irish market.
The next significant data ahead would be the U.S. employment cost index, due next Tuesday, and U.S. payrolls, due next Friday, dealers said.
Irish EBR figures and monetary statistics to be released next week would also be of interest.

Dealers said there had been some slackening of the curve on Wednesday, with the short end affected by a slight tightening of rates on the interbank market due to Irish pound-buying by the Central Bank.
The long end was in pretty good shape, dealers said, thanks in part to today's EU forecast for the Irish economy which was supportive of Irish entry into EMU.

On the Irish market at 1515 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 10 pence from Tuesday's close at 101.87 to yield 6.00 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 gained five pence to 108.45 to yield 6.73 percent.

Dealers said Irish bonds were yielding 147 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area - a widening of two basis points from Tuesday - and 90 basis points over bunds in the 10-year, a narrowing of one basis point.
